RoB 2 judgements from signalling questions

rob2_algorithm.Rd

Applies the RoB 2 algorithms to answers to the signalling questions and returns domain and overall risk of bias judgements, ready for rob_plot() and rob_summary(). Supports individually randomised parallel-group, cluster-randomised and crossover trials (RoB 2 cribsheets, 2019 and 2021), which can be mixed within one meta-analysis.

Usage

rob2_algorithm(
  data,
  design = "parallel",
  effect = c("assignment", "adhering"),
  keep_answers = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per study and one column per signalling question, named as in the RoB 2 cribsheets:

  • Domain 1: 1.1-1.3 (or 1a.1-1a.3).

  • Domain 1b (cluster trials): 1b.1-1b.3.

  • Domain S (crossover trials): S.1-S.3.

  • Domain 2: 2.1-2.7 (cluster trials, effect of assignment: 2.1a and 2.1b in place of 2.1).

  • Domain 3: 3.1-3.4 (cluster trials: 3.1a and 3.1b).

  • Domain 4: 4.1-4.5 (cluster trials: 4.3a and 4.3b).

  • Domain 5: 5.1-5.3 (crossover trials: also 5.4).

Prefixes and underscores are allowed (e.g. q1_1, D2.1a). Answers are Y, PY, PN, N or NI, abbreviated or in full (e.g. "Probably yes"). Leave questions the algorithm skips empty; a required question left empty is treated as "No information".

design

Trial design: "parallel" (default), "cluster" or "crossover". Either one value for all studies, or an unquoted column name giving the design of each study.

effect

Effect of interest for domain 2: "assignment" (the intention-to-treat effect, default) or "adhering" (the per-protocol effect).

keep_answers

Logical. Keep the signalling question columns? (default: FALSE).

Value

data with columns D1, (D1b), D2-D5, (DS) and Overall.

Details

Domain judgements follow the cribsheet algorithms. The overall judgement is "Low" if all domains are low risk, "High" if any domain is high risk, and "Some concerns" otherwise. The guidance allows "some concerns" in multiple domains to be judged high overall; edit Overall if you make that call.

D1b is returned only if there are cluster trials, and DS only if there are crossover trials. Both are NA for studies of other designs.

Examples

answers <- tibble::tibble(
  Author = c("Thermopolis", "Sachs", "Austen"),
  Year = c(2001, 2006, 2007),
  design = c("parallel", "cluster", "crossover"),
  `1.1` = c("Y", "Y", "PY"),
  `1.2` = c("Y", "PY", "NI"),
  `1.3` = c("N", "N", "N"),
  `1b.1` = c(NA, "N", NA),
  `1b.2` = c(NA, "PN", NA),
  `1b.3` = c(NA, "N", NA),
  `S.1` = c(NA, NA, "Y"),
  `S.3` = c(NA, NA, "PY"),
  `2.1` = c("N", NA, "Y"),
  `2.1a` = c(NA, "N", NA),
  `2.2` = c("N", "Y", "Y"),
  `2.3` = c(NA, "PN", "Y"),
  `2.4` = c(NA, NA, "PY"),
  `2.5` = c(NA, NA, "N"),
  `2.6` = c("Y", "Y", "PN"),
  `2.7` = c(NA, NA, "N"),
  `3.1` = c("Y", NA, "N"),
  `3.1a` = c(NA, "Y", NA),
  `3.1b` = c(NA, "PY", NA),
  `3.2` = c(NA, NA, "N"),
  `3.3` = c(NA, NA, "PY"),
  `3.4` = c(NA, NA, "PN"),
  `4.1` = c("N", "N", "N"),
  `4.2` = c("N", "N", "PN"),
  `4.3` = c("N", NA, "Y"),
  `4.3a` = c(NA, "PN", NA),
  `4.4` = c(NA, NA, "PY"),
  `4.5` = c(NA, NA, "PN"),
  `5.1` = c("Y", "N", "Y"),
  `5.2` = c("N", "N", "N"),
  `5.3` = c("N", "N", "PN"),
  `5.4` = c(NA, NA, "N"))

judged <- rob2_algorithm(answers, design = design)
judged
#> # A tibble: 3 × 11
#>   Author       Year design    D1     D1b   D2    D3    D4    D5    DS    Overall
#>   <chr>       <dbl> <chr>     <chr>  <chr> <chr> <chr> <chr> <chr> <chr> <chr>  
#> 1 Thermopolis  2001 parallel  Low    NA    Low   Low   Low   Low   NA    Low    
#> 2 Sachs        2006 cluster   Low    Low   Low   Low   Low   Some… NA    Some c…
#> 3 Austen       2007 crossover Some … NA    High  Some… Some… Low   Low   High   

rob_plot(judged, add_rob_legend = TRUE)
